formation.explanation: Caller append buffers or forwards until a leader is in Accept. The leader gathers matching per-node promises to a configured preparation quorum, selects maximum accepted round/length and maximum decided index, installs history, and synchronizes promised followers. Local appends update self support and emit AcceptDecide. Followers with matching promise, phase and sequence persist accepted entries and reply. Leader handle_accepted records sender support; a configured acceptance quorum at a larger index advances its decided prefix and propagates Decide or coalesced metadata. Followers advance decided state with batch handling; reads label entries below that index as Decided.

context.explanation: BLE heartbeat rounds and manual takeover nominate ballots. SequencePaxos acquires local preparation authority only above its prior leader and promise. Prepare flushes pending writes, persists the promise, resets receive sequence and returns accepted history. Matching promises enable transition to Accept. Higher Prepare changes follower authority; old-ballot acceptance is rejected with NotAccepted, unexplained future ballots and sequence gaps request recovery, outdated sequenced messages are ignored. Restart with stored promise enters Recover; reconnect and timer paths repeat preparation. A StopSign accepted as final entry blocks new appends, and its decision allows caller-created next-configuration instances.

connection.explanation: Authority changes constrain which accepted history can become new support: promises report accepted round/length and existing decision index; maximal history is installed before new proposals are accepted. Follower synchronization retains a prefix based on matching accepted rounds or decided history, then starts a new sequence session. A new leader resets volatile support; recovery retains persisted history and cannot simply reuse ordinary acceptance phase. Old-ballot messages are rejected, while same-ballot late promises trigger follower synchronization. Buffered ordinary proposals are appended by a winning leader or forwarded after follower sync unless sealed. Prior StopSign travels with history and blocks further appends. Same-ballot delayed replies, configuration routing and buffered StopSign transfer remain localized unresolved premises. The runtime adds a volatile EntryId-to-index/ballot assignment and consumes the core decided prefix to complete append_notify; its success branch precedes the supersession check, leaving late assignment identity across ballots unresolved.

grounding.derivation: The public method says append an entry and await its decided log index. The Superseded documentation permits stopping conservatively when a leader changes because the entry might still survive; this permits false-negative errors, not success for another value. Assignment records index and ballot at acceptance, while core consensus may replace unchosen values across ballots. Therefore success requires the requested entry, not solely a decided numeric position.
grounding.applicability: Use the original caller invocation, its real tagged EntryId and real assignment; correlate successful response with the live decided log at the same origin.
alternatives: Superseded or Timeout can satisfy the safety requirement without deciding the input.
If new leader retains the original value, successful notification is consistent with the requirement.
